agenda.title: Keep or remove the global allow rule Bash(export CC_AGENT=*)?
agenda.brief: Facts (from the agent-identity README, 2026-11-02): a global PreToolUse hook rewrites every Bash command a Claude Code agent runs to begin with `export CC_AGENT='<key> parent=... type=... depth=... src=agent-identity-hook/2'; `, so tools (vsect, git trailers) can read which agent acted. Claude Code's permission check runs on the rewritten command, so an allow rule `Bash(export CC_AGENT=*)` was added to ~/.claude/settings.json. Measured: without it, in default permission mode the export needed approval and ordinary allowed commands were refused. The README's argument that it is safe: the rule matches only the export; a command after it is judged on its own (a test `touch` still needed approval); `export CC_AGENT=$(...)` substitution is refused by the harness's export parser. Not verified: how two PreToolUse hooks that both rewrite Bash combine; what the TUI permission prompt shows. The rule was added by the implementing agent with the refactor lead's approval; it now waits on Joseph. Move what you would recommend to him (keep, remove, or keep with conditions).
